descripcion: At B2 the goal is to recognise and produce two clear registers — informal (contractions, phrasal verbs) and formal (no contractions, more Latinate vocabulary) — without mixing them in the same message. The finer six-axis control and full rewriting across three registers (C1) isn't the target yet.

filas: do not, it is, we are

ejemplos.texto: I regret that I am unable to attend this evening.

notas: Contractions are the fastest signal of informal register — removing them alone shifts a sentence towards formal.
Phrasal verbs (find out, sort out) are informal; their Latinate equivalents (discover, resolve) are formal.
Mixing registers within the same message — a contraction next to a very formal word — is the most common register error at this level.

contraste.es: Spanish marks formality mainly through tú/usted and verb forms, which English lacks. English carries register through vocabulary and contractions, so Spanish speakers who are polite with usted may still mix registers in English.
contraste.de: German marks formality with Sie, which English lacks. English carries register through vocabulary, contractions and forms like Could you…? versus Can you…?, so these need conscious attention.
contraste.it: Italian marks formality with Lei, which English lacks. English carries register through vocabulary, contractions and forms like Could you…? versus Can you…?.
contraste.fr: French marks formality with vous, which English lacks. English carries register through vocabulary, contractions and forms like Could you…? versus Can you…?.
contraste.pt: Portuguese marks formality with você or o senhor, which English lacks. English carries register through vocabulary, contractions and forms like Could you…? versus Can you…?.

errores: Mixing a contraction with a very formal word in the same sentence.
Using a phrasal verb in a formal email where its Latinate equivalent would fit better.
Assuming formal English is just longer or harder, rather than a different set of choices.

traducciones.fr: Je ne peux pas venir — désolé(e) !

redemittel.expresion: I regret that I am unable to…

traducciones.de: Ich bedaure, dass ich nicht… kann.
traducciones.fr: Je regrette de ne pas pouvoir…

redemittel.expresion: Please do not hesitate to contact me.

traducciones.de: Bitte zögern Sie nicht, mich zu kontaktieren.

autochequeo: Are contractions used consistently, either all present or all absent?
Are phrasal verbs replaced with formal equivalents in the formal version?
Is the register consistent throughout, without mixing?
Would the intended reader find the register appropriate?
Have I written the same content in both registers to compare?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on register. Check for mixed formal and informal features in the same message, especially contractions next to formal vocabulary. Do not rewrite the text.
